content: For me I was already on 8.0.0 before the update and even with the INDX firmware on the USB it didnt recognise it as a new/different version so had to force the update through Connect

replies.content: i was on core one + v8 firmware, downloaded the matching v8 indx firmware after a gen 2 and indx upgrade.  new firmware was not recognised and ended up having to force a hard factory reset

I had the same thing. For me, what I did was I removed all other .bbf files from the flash drive, reset/power cycled the printer, then held the knob down while it booted. That forced it to pick up the new firmware.
For me it was double clicking the knob, when the prusa logo appeared after the reset.

content: I used 6.9.2 from https://github.com/prusa3d/Prusa-Firmware-Buddy/releases/tag/v6.9.2 - after flashing it detected the INDX automatically and then started the wizard.
I had the same issue as Stephen. Go to Prusa CORE One/+ INDX support page, and get THAT firmware.  I only had the Core One/+/Gen2 firmware.

um COREONEINDX was not listed as an option and I definitely have this driver https://help.prusa3d.com/product/core-one-indx flashed...
It gave me the option of the COREONEGEN2 but I can't go back from the calibration screen to get to that...
